description: THE PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION DECISION as DATA (self-improvement, EFFICIENCY branch). The prior build GUESSED a cache to make Wikipedia loading faster -- blind, because the jabberwock could not SEE its load timing. Now it PERCEIVES its load timing (LatencyObservation nodes, domains/load_timing.py) and DECIDES the fix from that perception. The ONE decision -- given a perceived performance gap, what SHAPE is the cost and which fix does that shape call for -- is NOT a Python if/else; it is these two graph-resident Programs (the twin of seeds/research_agenda_dispatch.json's route_pick and seeds/composer_dispatch.json's composer_pick). perf_diagnose reads the gap's COLD-vs-WARM fields (cold_ms of the dominant stage, warm cost per item) and returns the cost SHAPE: IfThenElse(Gt(Div(cold, warm), RATIO), 'one-time-init', 'per-item') -- when the first (cold) call dwarfs the steady per-item cost, one-time init DOMINATES; else the cost is genuinely per-item. perf_fix_pick then maps that shape to its fix via an Argmin-by-priority over the PerfFixCue nodes whose shape Eq the diagnosed shape (the SAME Filter/Argmin/Attr shape route_pick uses): one-time-init -> warm_once, per-item -> optimize-op. There is DELIBERATELY no PerfFixCue mapping any shape to a cache: a cache amortizes PER-ITEM repetition, which the diagnosis says is NOT the shape of a one-time init -- so the agent, reading its OWN timing through these Programs, never SELECTS a cache. RATIO=50: a cold init >= 50x the warm per-item cost is one-time-init (real WordNet: ~1400ms cold / ~0.4ms warm = 3500x, far over; a per-item-shaped cost has cold ~ warm, far under).

microtheory.name: performance_optimization
microtheory.description: which fix a perceived performance gap calls for, keyed on the SHAPE of its cost (one-time init -> warm_once; per-item -> optimize-op; never a cache for a one-time init).

attrs.rationale: the cost is a one-time init dwarfing the per-item cost -> pay it once up front (warm the corpus); NOT a cache (nothing per-item repeats to amortize).
the cost is genuinely per-item -> optimize the repeated op itself.
